systems.title: Machine Learning
systems.goal: Build a supervised classifier from a labeled dataset and prove it generalizes beyond the training data.
systems.data: A versioned table with features, target label, train/validation/test split, and a data dictionary.
systems.baseline: Start with a simple linear/logistic or tree baseline before increasing model complexity.
steps: Define the prediction target and decision cost
Validate data schema and split before feature work
Evaluate once on held-out test data
Package preprocessing and model together for inference
metrics: Accuracy only when class/cost balance justifies it
systems.starter:
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression

model = make_pipeline(StandardScaler(), LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(model.score(X_valid, y_valid))

systems.title: Deep Learning
systems.goal: Train a neural network with a reproducible data pipeline, validation loop, checkpoint, and failure diagnostics.
systems.data: Versioned tensors or dataset objects with training/validation separation and deterministic preprocessing.
systems.baseline: Use the smallest network that can overfit a tiny batch; then scale only after the training loop is known to work.
steps: Overfit a tiny batch as a wiring test
Plot loss/metric curves and inspect errors
production: Use reproducible seeds only as debugging aids
systems.starter:
import torch
from torch import nn

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(n_features, 64), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(64, n_classes))
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

systems.title: Large Language Models
systems.goal: Build and evaluate a small causal language-model pipeline, then scale through fine-tuning or retrieval without hiding the inference mechanics.
stack: Hugging Face Transformers for practical models
systems.data: Tokenized, licensed text with train/validation separation, provenance, quality filters, and task-specific evaluation examples.
systems.baseline: Use an n-gram or tiny causal transformer to verify tokenization, masking, loss, decoding, and evaluation before using a large pretrained model.
steps: Choose tokenizer and inspect token statistics
Train or load a small baseline
Add retrieval/fine-tuning only for a defined failure
Measure latency, KV-cache memory, safety and regression behavior
production: Version model, tokenizer, prompt and retrieval corpus
Apply guardrails and human review for consequential actions
systems.starter:
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

name = 'distilgpt2'
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(name)
inputs = tok('Engineering evidence matters because', return_tensors='pt')
print(tok.decode(model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=20)[0]))

systems.title: Agentic AI
systems.goal: Build an agent loop where model decisions, tools, state, approvals, and evidence are separate observable components.
stack: An agent SDK or explicit Responses/tool loop
systems.data: Task/evaluation cases, tool schemas, permission policy, and recorded traces rather than a training dataset alone.
systems.baseline: One agent, one bounded read-only tool, explicit stop condition, and an evaluation set.
steps: Define the task boundary and success criteria
Create one agent with narrow instructions
Add stop/loop limits and error handling
Trace every tool call and result
Evaluate task success, safety, cost and recovery behavior
systems.starter:
from agents import Agent, Runner

agent = Agent(name='Analyst', instructions='Use tools only when required; cite evidence.')
result = Runner.run_sync(agent, 'Summarize the bounded test case')
print(result.final_output)

systems.title: Computer Vision
systems.goal: Build an image classifier or detector with reproducible transforms, error analysis, and a baseline that exposes dataset problems.
systems.data: Versioned labeled images with class definitions, split policy, licensing, and augmentation rules.
systems.baseline: A small CNN or pretrained feature extractor with a frozen baseline.
steps: Define image task and label policy

systems.title: Reinforcement Learning
systems.goal: Build an agent in a bounded environment and verify learning against a simple policy baseline.
systems.data: Environment transitions and reward signals; evaluation episodes must use fixed seeds/scenarios separate from training.
systems.baseline: Random policy, heuristic policy, or tabular Q-learning before deep RL.
steps: Define state, actions, transition and reward
Write environment invariants and termination rules
Plot return and stability across seeds
Add safety constraints before real-world actuation
production: Bound actions and terminate unsafe states
Never infer safety from reward alone
systems.starter: import numpy as np\nQ = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))\nQ[s,a] += alpha * (reward + gamma * Q[next_s].max() - Q[s,a])

systems.title: Generative AI
systems.goal: Build a bounded generative model or decoder and evaluate both fidelity and diversity instead of relying on attractive samples.
systems.data: Licensed, versioned generation corpus plus a held-out evaluation set and safety exclusions.
systems.baseline: A simple autoregressive or autoencoder-style model that makes likelihood/reconstruction behavior inspectable.
steps: Define generation target and acceptable output space
Document sampling controls and failure cases
production: Rate-limit and moderate high-risk use cases

systems.title: Multimodal AI
systems.goal: Build separate modality encoders and a measurable fusion strategy, then test what happens when one modality is missing or wrong.
systems.data: Aligned examples across modalities with explicit missing-modality and disagreement cases.
systems.baseline: Late fusion of independent modality scores before training a joint model.
production: Fallback when a modality is unavailable
systems.starter: # Start with explicit late fusion\nfused_score = text_weight * text_score + (1-text_weight) * vision_score\nassert 0 <= fused_score <= 1

systems.title: Symbolic AI
systems.goal: Build an explicit fact/rule system whose conclusions can be traced and tested.
systems.data: Facts, rules, and expected inference cases with contradiction/edge cases.
systems.baseline: Forward-chaining rules over a small fact set.
steps: Add persistence or a solver only if needed
production: Validate rule changes with regression cases
systems.starter: facts = {'authorized': True, 'encrypted': True}\nrules = [('allow', lambda f: f.get('authorized') and f.get('encrypted'))]\nprint([name for name, rule in rules if rule(facts)])

systems.title: Neuro-symbolic AI
systems.goal: Combine a learned scorer with explicit constraints and measure both task performance and rule violations.
systems.data: Labeled examples plus constraint tests that intentionally include high-confidence rule violations.
systems.baseline: Neural score followed by a hard constraint gate.
steps: Combine neural decision with constraint layer
Decide whether rules veto, re-rank, or provide features
production: Test both layers during every release
systems.starter: neural_ok = score >= threshold\nconstraint_ok = all(rule(example) for rule in rules)\nfinal = neural_ok and constraint_ok

systems.title: Multi-agent Systems
systems.goal: Build multiple bounded specialists with explicit ownership, coordination, shared-state rules, and evaluation of handoffs.
systems.data: Task suite containing cases for each specialist plus ambiguous/handoff cases.
systems.baseline: Manager agent calls two specialists as tools; no peer-to-peer autonomy initially.
steps: Evaluate coordination cost versus single-agent baseline
production: Keep one owner for side effects
Compare multi-agent value to a simpler single-agent design
systems.starter: # Pseudocode boundary\nmanager = Agent(name='manager', tools=[researcher.as_tool(), verifier.as_tool()])\n# Evaluate whether delegation improves task success before adding more agents.

systems.title: AI Memory & Retrieval
systems.goal: Build a retrieval pipeline with chunking, indexing, ranking, citation, freshness, and measurable recall.
systems.data: Versioned source documents, chunk metadata, timestamps, and a query set with expected relevant passages.
systems.baseline: TF-IDF/cosine retrieval before embeddings or reranking.
production: Treat retrieved text as untrusted data

systems.title: Embodied / Robotic AI
systems.goal: Build a simulation-first perception/state/control loop with explicit safety limits before connecting learning to physical actuation.
systems.data: Simulated sensor/state trajectories, command limits, and scenario suite including failures.
systems.baseline: Proportional or finite-state controller before learned control.
steps: Gate hardware actions with safety controller
systems.starter: error = target - current\ncommand = max(-limit, min(limit, kp * error))\n# Learned policy must remain inside an independent safety envelope.

systems.title: Game AI
systems.goal: Build a decision system for a game and compare rule-based, search, and learned policies using measurable gameplay outcomes.
systems.data: Game states/scenarios, legal actions, outcome labels or reward logs.
systems.baseline: Finite-state behavior or minimax/search before learned policies.
steps: Define game state and legal actions
Add stochastic/learned policy only when justified
production: Validate every chosen action against game rules

systems.title: Geometric AI
systems.goal: Build features/models that respect known geometric transformations and verify invariance/equivariance numerically.
systems.data: Geometric objects plus transformed copies with known transformation labels.
systems.baseline: Hand-designed invariant features or augmentation baseline.
production: Keep provenance for upstream research code
Separate research claim from demo behavior

systems.title: Graph Neural Networks
systems.goal: Build a message-passing baseline on a graph and evaluate whether graph structure improves the task over non-graph baselines.
systems.data: Nodes, edges, node/edge features, labels, and train/validation/test splits that avoid leakage across graph structure.
systems.baseline: Mean/sum neighbor aggregation or non-graph feature model.
systems.starter: neighbor_mean = sum(neighbor_features) / max(1, len(neighbor_features))\nupdated = self_feature + neighbor_mean

systems.title: Personal Development Agent
systems.goal: Build a personal assistant that separates read/suggest behavior from consequential actions and keeps memory/provenance inspectable.
stack: Agent framework or explicit tool loop
systems.data: User-authorized notes/tasks/preferences with provenance and deletion/update semantics.
systems.baseline: Read + suggest only; no autonomous side effects.
steps: Define allowed data and action scopes
Evaluate privacy, accuracy and task completion
systems.starter: if action in {'modify','send'} and not approved:\n    raise PermissionError('human approval required')\nreturn suggest(context)

systems.title: Project MIND
systems.goal: Build an evidence-first technical agent workflow where planning, artifacts, verification, and proposed actions are independently inspectable.
systems.data: Task requests, typed artifacts, acceptance criteria, verifier results, and versioned attempts.
systems.baseline: Deterministic planner + evidence ledger + verifier before live tools.
systems.starter: result = {'plan': plan(task), 'artifacts': []}\nfor artifact in execute_dry_run(result['plan']):\n    result['artifacts'].append({'data': artifact, 'verified': verify(artifact)})

systems.title: Build Your Own AI
systems.goal: Choose the smallest AI system that can answer a well-defined task, then prove it beats a baseline before adding complexity.
stack: Choose only what the task requires
systems.data: A documented input/output contract, examples, held-out evaluation cases, and provenance/licensing.
systems.baseline: Rules, search, statistical baseline, or existing model before custom training.
steps: Add complexity for a measured failure
